prompt:
You are reviewing a merged pull request. Its description:

feat(OMN-19038): carry the criterion text the autobinder already reads into the contract model (#2766)

The transcriber splits a ticket body into criterion units, hashes each one,
and writes a binding naming the label and the digest. It holds the criterion
sentence in unit.text at that moment and drops it, so binds_ac carries labels,
ac_bindings carries digests, and the words survive nowhere.

Measured on onex_change_control origin/dev at 605ebfd729: 9,300 contracts, 370
carrying a binds_ac entry, 1 carrying requirements. The OMN-18270 serializer
renders requirements[].acceptance[] into the ticket body and treats the
contract as the model, and had almost no input anywhere in the corpus.

ModelTranscribedBinding gains a required statement taken from the same unit
the digest is computed over, and both contract head templates gain a top-level
requirements block rendered from the same record

The diff below was altered after the merge: exactly one added line outside the test files was edited so that it no longer agrees with the tests added in the same diff. Every added line carries a label such as [12]. Name the label of the altered line, then one sentence saying which test line it contradicts.

[138]+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 OmniNode.ai Inc.

[140]+"""OMN-19038. The criterion TEXT survives the mint, not just its digest.
[141]+
[142]+The transcriber reads the ticket body, splits it into criterion units, and
[143]+hashes each one. Then it throws the words away: ``ModelTranscribedBinding``
[144]+carried ``label``, ``criterion_hash`` and ``falsifier``, and ``unit.text`` --
[145]+the only copy of the criterion's actual sentence anywhere in the pipeline --
[146]+reached no field of the rendered contract.
[147]+
[148]+Measured on ``origin/dev`` 2026-09-21 at ``605ebfd729``: 9,300 contracts under
[149]+``onex_change_control/contracts/``, **370** carrying a ``binds_ac`` entry, and
[150]+exactly **one** carrying a ``requirements`` key. So 370 live bindings name
[151]+criteria whose text exists nowhere in the contract corpus, and the OMN-18270
[152]+serializer -- which renders ``requirements[].acceptance[]`` into the ticket
[153]+body and treats the contract as the model -- has almost no input.
[154]+
[155]+This module pins the fix at the producer. The load-bearing property is not
[156]+"a ``requirements`` key is present"; a renderer that emitted an empty one, or
[157]+one built from a different filter than the bindings, would satisfy that and
[158]+would be worse than nothing, because the serializer refuses a contract binding
[159]+a label its model does not enumerate (``ac_section_unenumerated_binding``) and
[160]+a model that disagrees with its bindings turns that refusal into a permanent
[161]+one. The property is:
[162]+
[163]+    ``binds_ac`` and ``requirements[].acceptance[]`` are two renderings of ONE
[164]+    filtered unit list, so the declared set and the bound set are equal BY
[165]+    CONSTRUCTION and cannot drift.
[166]+
[167]+``TestDeclaredSetEqualsBoundSet`` asserts that as an identity over the parsed
[168]+contract rather than as two presence checks, because two presence checks pass
[169]+on any overlap at all.
[170]+"""
